description_en: Astūpafrom the mid-14th century.The monument is located on a small hill north-west of the villages of Śrīḍhuskā and Umgāḍ, where are found 14 stone memorial pillars (JUM0200). Opposite the hill, to the west, is a similar elevation on which is built a stone pavilion (baiṭhak,JUM0100).Thestūpawas in a derelict consition when it was last surveyed, in April 2022. It had visibly been dismantled and partly (and poorly) re-assembled. The original structure was built on a square platform with receeding steps leading to a cubical volume. The latter had a central salient horizontal moulding. Above were three receeding steps, topped by a dome. Thestūpa's sides are oriented to the north, east, south and west.On the eastern side, the central projection on the cubic volume contains an low relief inscription. It readsOṃ maṇi padme hūṃ, Avalokiteśvara's mantra, in Rañjana script. The epigraphy is identical to the one seen on the same mantra inscribed on Dullu's Kīrtikhambā (DLK0260), the Patharnauli reservoir (DLK0160). Both monuments were built in the 1350's, during the rule of king Pṛthvīmalla (r. 1338-1358) (Andolfatto 2019, p. 96;Pant 2009, 301). It is likely that the Śrīḍhuskā Stūpa was built around the same period.The monument is briefly described inSharma 2012, p. 185.
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number JUM0110_I

historical_events.event_description: The mantraOṃ maṇi padme hūṃis engraved in low relief on the eastern side of the stūpa. It is inscribed in Rañjana script.It does not bar a date but it is possible to compare it with other inscriptions, dated from the 1350's.
